review_candidates.description: The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems. CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic, with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally. At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Working closely with the National Department of Health (NDoH), NACS, Provincial Health Authorities, partners, and the relevant technical working groups and committees, the Associate, HIV Prevention will Support planning, organisation, communication, risk mapping, monitoring and quality execution of CHAI's LEN PrEP activities in line with CHAI's values and policies. In collaboration with HIV partners, update the LEN forecast each quarter using consumption and uptake data and market intelligence on generic supply, prices and pack sizes, so that requisitions keep pace with demand. Support NDoH to finalise LEN indicators and data tools, integrate them into eNHIS, and follow up on data quality. Analyse data on PrEP uptake, continuation, consumption and demand generation, and prepare analysis for HIV TWG reviews to guide program improvements and expansion. Support pharmacovigilance and adverse event reporting for LEN. Strengthen routine monitoring, learning and documentation processes, and build simple dashboards that program teams and government counterparts can use. Build and maintain strong working relationships with government counterparts, international agencies, donors, NGO partners and civil society, ensuring coordinated implementation and reporting of activities. Represent CHAI PNG in national and regional forums, promoting the exchange of best practices and program learning. Develop and disseminate knowledge products, lessons learned and progress reports, including reports to Unitaid and Wits RHI. Work closely with CHAI's global HIV Prevention team to align with global standards and share lessons with NDoH and partners. Identify and assess project risks and challenges, and provide evidence-based recommendations to the Program Manager. Contribute to broader CHAI PNG initiatives within the INCDs cluster, including forecasting and quantification support for other essential medicines and diagnostics as needed. Perform any other duties as needed by the program and validated by the manager.
